question: Balancing Uber's 20% Gross Bookings scale against its M&A leverage pivot, UK VAT cash drag, AV threats, and Stage 4 breakdown, what is our exact decision?

epigraph.quote: Great companies can still be rejected stocks when capital allocation shifts toward empire-building and the tape breaks into Stage 4.
epigraph.author: Institutional Capital Allocation Playbook

web_blocks.html: An honest call weighs both sides of the debate before setting rules. On the Bull side, Uber stays a strong habit engine. Monthly users hit 215 million (+14% YoY) and quarterly trips reached 4,061 million (+16% YoY) [31, 32]. Q3 2026 Gross Bookings grew 20% YoY to $59.82 billion, and Q4 guidance sits at $63.25B–$65.25B [32]. Trailing Free Cash Flow hit $10.42 billion on just 0.6% capex intensity [31]. Uber One (>50 million members) and Advertising (>$2.5 billion run-rate) deepen engagement [3, 19]. Bulls argue robotaxis will plug into Uber's demand graph to fill off-peak hours [18].

On the Bear side, Pass 1 uncovered hard financial and strategic risks [31]. First, Waymo runs its own ride-hailing app alongside Uber, while Tesla and Zoox build closed-loop fleets [31]. Second, management cut quarterly buybacks 75% from $3,010 million in Q1 to $754 million in Q3 [31]. Cash pivoted to a ~$14.8 billion Delivery Hero bid and a $2.3 billion ezCater deal [31, 33]. Long-term debt jumped 49% to $15,664 million with €18.2 billion in loan lines [31, 34, 35]. Third, UK HMRC demands another $1.5 billion cash appeal outflow on a $3.4 billion VAT bill [31]. Also, $13.71 billion in insurance reserves locks up $11.37 billion in restricted cash, and Australia ruled against Uber on payroll tax [31]. With shares in Stage 4 at $63.47 during a 10-day US Downtrend, buying here breaks both trend and cash-flow rules.

book_paragraphs: We have reached our final judgment, where Pass 1's business and balance-sheet forensics, Pass 2's SBC-adjusted DCF, and the November 20, 2026 Stage 4 tape converge into one disciplined verdict. Let us put both sides of the aisle side by side before locking in our rules.

On the Bull side, Uber's core marketplace demand remains impressive. Monthly Active Platform Consumers reached 215 million (+14% YoY), trips hit 4,061 million (+16% YoY), Q3 Gross Bookings rose 20% to $59.82 billion, and Q4 guidance calls for $63.25 billion to $65.25 billion. Over 50 million Uber One members and a $2.5 billion-plus Advertising run-rate lock in high-frequency engagement while keeping capital intensity at just 0.6% of revenue. If autonomous fleets ultimately plug into Uber's demand graph to maximize off-peak utilization, Uber's cash engine can compound for years.

On the Bear side, however, the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q introduced four hard frictions that change the near-term risk/reward. First, Waymo already runs a competing first-party app alongside Tesla and Zoox, risking both customer disintermediation and partner take-rate compression. Second, management pivoted from pure share buybacks—slashing repurchases 75% from $3.01 billion in Q1 to $754 million in Q3—to launch a $14.8 billion Delivery Hero takeover and $2.3 billion ezCater deal, pushing long-term debt up 49% to $15.66 billion. Third, UK HMRC's $3.4 billion back-VAT dispute requires another $1.5 billion cash appeal outflow, while $13.71 billion in insurance reserves locks up $11.37 billion in restricted cash and Australia's High Court ruled against Uber on payroll taxes. Fourth, Uber's stock sits in a full Stage 4 breakdown at $63.47—12.32% below its 200-day average—during a 10-distribution-day US market Downtrend.

Pricing those forces into our SBC-adjusted pro-forma DCF yields a $45.00 Bear target (30% weight, -29.1%), a $75.00 Base target (50% weight, +18.2%), and a $108.00 Bull target (20% weight, +70.2%), weighting to a $72.60 expected value (+14.4%). Stripping the unclosed +$0.45 billion M&A FCF credit trims Base to $70.14 ($65.50 after -$0.48 billion debt/legal drag), while combined Bear stress incorporating the $2.34 billion uncollateralized insurance gap cuts Bear fair value to $41.78 (-34.2%). Because Uber is locked in Stage 4 (CAP_REJECTED), our New-Capital Verdict is REJECTED (TIER_0; reasons: TREND and CASH_FLOW). We assign 0.0% bids, treat the $61.24–$63.10 band ($60.96 stop) strictly as a historical technical support reference below the $63.00 LEAPS floor, and require a full Stage 1 base plus Stage 2 reclaim above $73.50 first.

Across our three investment horizons, the rules are unambiguous. Over 1 to 12 weeks, Reject / Stay Away while 1.63x distribution volume presses shares near $63.29 lows. Over 3 to 12 months, REJECTED (TIER_0) keeps fresh dollars out of a falling knife. Over 2 to 5 years, Uber keeps its COMPOUNDER_PASS quality rating with PASS_WITH_WATCH, awaiting proof of Delivery Hero debt paydown (<2.0x) and autonomous take-rate stability.

Look closely at why 100% of marginal cash remains in CASH today. Consolidated US cash stands at just $2,540.35—only 3.38% of our $75,110.60 net worth—far below the 22.0% cash floor prescribed during a 10-distribution-day market Downtrend. Even though unheld shortlist candidate AbbVie ($286.20, Stage 2, $340.00 Base target, 1.85:1 asymmetry) and outside insurance candidate Arch Capital Group ($108.82, Stage 2, $130.00 Base target, 1.85:1 asymmetry) trade in healthy uptrends, both stay unfunded at 0% until portfolio cash reserves recover.

Finally, let us restate our exact existing-position protocol with zero ambiguity. Equity accounts hold zero common Uber shares (NOT_HELD, holding_shares_to_sell: 0). For our 5 open Dec 17, 2027 LEAPS contracts in Robinhood—4x $110C and 1x $100C, carrying $3,463.86 cost, $1,775.86 prior market value, 392 DTE as of November 20, 2026, and ~$820–$1,020 Black-Scholes value—we mandate EXIT_IMMEDIATELY (CLOSE_INTO_CASH). Both strikes expire at $0.00 intrinsic value at our $75.00 Base Case, $63.47 sits 47 cents above $63.00 on 1.63x Stage 4 volume with >14% spreads, and US cash is 3.38% versus the 22.0% floor. Close all 5 contracts cleanly on market liquidity into USD cash, with zero averaging down and hard invalidation <= $63.00.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: WHY REJECTED PROTECTS COMPOUNDING
book_callouts.text: Rejecting a good business when its chart enters Stage 4 and management pivots into debt-funded M&A is capital preservation. By keeping 100% of marginal dollars in cash and closing the 5 out-of-the-money Dec 2027 LEAPS immediately into USD cash, you eliminate gap-down and theta decay risk while rebuilding starved liquidity.
